newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Former chief justice tops Hong Kong leader poll. [corrected 13:38 gmt]
newsitem.headline: Former chief justice tops Hong Kong leader poll. [corrected 13:38 gmt]

text.p: Former Hong Kong chief justice Ti Liang Yang would become the territory's first chief executive if the post was to be decided by an election, an opinion poll released on Thursday showed.
The telephone survey was conducted by the University of Hong Kong Social Science Research Centre, which interviewed 522 people between November 5 and 6 (Corrects days from November 15 and 16).

It said Yang would receive 33.5 percent of votes. Shipping tycoon Tung Chee-hwa, who has been tipped as Beijing's favourite, got 32.4 percent backing. Businessman Peter Woo mustered four percent and former Appeal Court judge Simon Li had only two percent support, the survey showed.
But popularity polls count for little in the contest to succeed Governor Chris Patten at midnight on June 30 when China resumes control of the colony ruled by Britain for more than 150 years.
The Chief Executive will be chosen by a 400-strong China-appointed Selection Committee in Hong Kong on December 11.
